vectors.name: compat/basic/adding-optional-field-narrows-forward
vectors.comment: A may emit `nick`; B is closed and has no such field. Readers holding B would break.

vectors.name: compat/basic/adding-optional-field-widens-backward
vectors.comment: The same pair, arguments reversed. Direction is the whole question.

vectors.name: compat/basic/adding-required-field-is-not-accepted-by-old
vectors.comment: Clause 2 of record_sub: B requires `email` with min 1 and A does not guarantee it.

vectors.name: compat/scalar/date-is-not-a-subtype-of-datetime
vectors.comment: integer/number is the ONLY subtyping relation. This vector exists to stop a fourth implementation from adding a second one.

vectors.name: compat/cardinality/unbounded-does-not-fit-bounded
vectors.comment: Also pins the comma-first cardinality form [,5], which the OSD grammar accepts.

vectors.name: compat/recursion/coinduction-terminates-on-mutual-refs
vectors.comment: Recursive on both sides. An implementation without memoized coinduction does not terminate here.

vectors.name: compat/satisfiability/unsatisfiable-a-is-vacuously-a-subschema
vectors.comment: A accepts no finite document, so every document it accepts is trivially accepted by B.

vectors.name: equivalent/renaming-records-preserves-equivalence
vectors.comment: Equivalence is about accepted documents, never about record names or declaration order.

vectors.name: equivalent/unsatisfiable-schemas-are-equivalent-vacuously
vectors.comment: Both schemas are unsatisfiable: every reference is mandatory, so each demands an infinitely deep document and neither accepts a finite one. Sec6.7 defines equivalence as accepting the same set of documents, and both accept the empty set, so they are equivalent vacuously -- despite differing in record names, record count, and field labels, none of which any document could expose. An implementation that errors or returns false on unsatisfiable input fails here while passing every other equivalent vector, since the existing two both use satisfiable schemas. Sec6.8's scope limitation and its Theorem 4 precondition both rest on this behavior.

vectors.name: equivalent/duplicated-records-equal-one-shared-record
vectors.comment: Three records versus two, and a different reference graph, but the same accepted documents. Sec6.7 forbids substituting structural equality for equivalence, and the two existing vectors only cover naming and reachability differences -- neither covers a differing record count. An implementation requiring a bijection between record sets, which is a natural reading of 'same structure', returns false here and passes every other vector.

vectors.name: equivalent/unemittable-optional-field-does-not-change-the-language
vectors.comment: The two schemas declare different field sets, and are still equivalent. U is unsatisfiable, so the optional field opt can never be emitted by any document, and B's language is exactly A's. This is the equivalence case most likely to be implemented wrongly: comparing declared field sets -- 'every field of A must appear in B and vice versa' -- is reasonable-looking and returns false here. Paired with the sibling vector below, which keeps the shape and makes U satisfiable, so the field becomes emittable and the answer flips.

vectors.name: equivalent/emittable-optional-field-does-change-the-language
vectors.comment: The negative boundary for the vector above: identical shape, except U's self-reference is now optional, so U is satisfiable and opt can actually be emitted. B therefore accepts documents A rejects, and the two are not equivalent. Pinning both sides matters because an implementation that simply ignores optional fields would pass the positive case for the wrong reason and fail here.
